clue.text: Dance with sergeant, say, on fire

blocks.note: a flame is fire
a sergeant is an example of a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A soldier of some rank, fired up, joins in a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the sergeant after the fire in the across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the passionate Spanish dance style from Andalusia.

clue.text: Build a number

blocks.note: first meaning: a person's physique
second meaning: a numeral

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests constructing a number; really the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure is someone's bodily shape, and also a written digit such as 7.

clue.text: Inherited a northern castle (close to Lancaster) in ruins

indicators.note: something in ruins has fallen apart, so the letters must be rebuilt in another order
'close to' keeps only the last letter of 'Lancaster'

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern
taken as written
the closing letter of Lancaster

explanation.surface: Someone inherits a ruined castle in the north near Lancaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ancestral has come down from one's forebears, i.e. been inherited.

clue.text: Feeling generated by Ernest's first proposal

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the name before it

blocks.note: the initial of Ernest
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: Ernest's marriage proposal stirs strong feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a feeling such as joy or fear; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Taking the easy option on finding problems supporting excavation

indicators.note: in a down entry, what is supporting sits underneath, so the problems come second, below the dig

blocks.note: a cutting is a trench dug through ground, e.g. for a railway
tight corners are awkward situations or problems

explanation.surface: Someone shirks effort when problems arise on a dig.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'supporting' puts the problems underneath the excavation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting corners is the idiom for doing something the quickest, cheapest way, skimping on care.

clue.text: Playing well, batting instead of Middlesex's opener

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so only the initial letter of the county is wanted

blocks.note: a batsman who is batting is in
for can mean in place of
first letter of Middlesex

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a batter in good form replaces Middlesex's opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture makes 'opener' look like the batsman; it only picks a letter. Middlesex is an English county cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsperson in form is performing at their best, i.e. playing well.

clue.text: Bewilder small number with new perk

blocks.note: NO is the short form of number
N is the abbreviation for new
a plus is an added benefit

explanation.surface: A small count paired with a fresh fringe benefit leaves someone puzzled.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to perplex them so they don't know how to respond.

clue.text: Command from frontier bishop ignored

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so the churchman's letter is dropped

blocks.note: a border is a frontier
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An order issued from the border, with the bishop paying no heed.
explanation.definitionFit: An order is an instruction given with authority, so a command.

clue.text: Fail to catch service, according to drunkard in a muddle?

indicators.note: a drunk slurs speech, turning each crisp hiss into a mushy sh sound

blocks.note: to miss is to fail to catch
Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A tipsy churchgoer confusedly says he missed Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'According to drunkard' tells you to pronounce each S as a drunken SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishmash is a confused jumble of things, a muddle.

clue.text: Broadcast he feared unwise, being so long

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A man worried that a broadcast was ill-advised.
explanation.definitionFit: Auf Wiedersehen is German for goodbye, as is the casual farewell 'so long'.

clue.text: Try holding nameless pet lizard

indicators.note: lacking a name means the abbreviation for name is removed
holding means one word grips the other inside it

blocks.note: to have a go is to try
to neck is to pet or kiss
N stands for name

explanation.surface: A suggestion to try keeping an unnamed pet lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like a household animal; it is the verb for kissing and cuddling.
explanation.definitionFit: A gecko is a small lizard with sticky toe pads, sometimes kept as a pet.

clue.text: Dish done differently in French city by Italian composer

indicators.note: done differently means the word is rearranged
in places the rearranged word inside the city's name

blocks.note: Tours is a city on the Loire
the four letters rearranged
Gioachino Rossini, composer of The Barber of Seville

explanation.surface: A dish cooked a different way in a French city by an Italian composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The dish really is named after Rossini, so the composer is both wordplay and part of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tournedos Rossini is a classic French preparation of beef fillet with foie gras and truffle.

clue.text: See 11
Heavy metal stuff by Austrian composer

blocks.note: Hugo Wolf, Austrian song composer
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Heavy metal music produced by an Austrian composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' looks like rock music; it is the chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is another name for tungsten, a very dense metallic element.

clue.text: Arresting son, surprisingly admitting extremely serious crimes

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the outermost letters of the next word
surprisingly suggests an unexpected outcome, so the words come out jumbled
admitting means letting something in, so other letters go inside

blocks.note: taken as written for the shuffle
the first and last letters of serious

explanation.surface: A police story: arresting a son for very serious crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Transgressions are breaches of law or rules, so crimes or offences.

clue.text: Main place for the rest of the natives?

definitions.text: Main place for the rest of the natives?

blocks.clueFragment: Main place for the rest of the natives?
blocks.note: surface reading: the principal spot where local people relax

blocks.clueFragment: Main place for the rest of the natives?
blocks.note: setter's reading: main is the sea, natives are farmed oysters, and the rest is where they lie

explanation.walkthrough: Natives are a variety of British oyster, and the main is an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An area of seabed where shellfish grow or are cultivated is where these molluscs lie.

clue.text: Pair watch, perhaps, for an unfaithful lover

blocks.note: a pair is two
a watch is an example of a timing device

explanation.surface: Two watches given as a gift to a cheating partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-timer secretly dates two people at once, being unfaithful.

clue.text: Each side slow at sea, around turn, in fruitless pursuit

indicators.note: at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are rearranged
around means the other letters are placed about the short word

blocks.note: taken as written for the shuffle
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Two slow sides at sea circle about, pursuing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild goose chase is the idiom for a hopeless search that achieves nothing.

clue.text: Young bird shot by catapult

blocks.note: a shot is an attempt, a go
a sling hurls stones like a catapult

explanation.surface: A young bird hit by a catapult shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like the firing; it means an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A gosling is a baby goose, a young bird.

clue.text: Who knows workers at university?

blocks.note: hands are manual workers
a student up at Oxford or Cambridge is in residence

explanation.surface: A question about which university workers are well informed.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher asks 'Who knows?' meaning raise your hand if you know the answer, the same as calling 'Hands up'.

clue.text: Fools appearing before singular judge

blocks.note: asses are fools
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Fools appear in court before a lone judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' looks like a magistrate noun; here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to evaluate or form an opinion of something, i.e. judge it.

clue.text: Puts up covers

blocks.note: first meaning: gives lodging to a guest
second meaning: includes or encompasses

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests hanging curtains or sheets; the two phrases are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Takes in can mean accommodates someone, and also includes a range of things.

clue.text: More than one toy aircraft

blocks.note: first meaning: several of the toys flown on a string
second meaning: old slang for planes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy aircraft' reads as one phrase; the split is after 'toy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kites are flying playthings, and kite was RAF slang for an aeroplane.

clue.text: Boy takes home poems

blocks.note: a son is a boy
to net is to earn as take-home pay

explanation.surface: A boy brings home some poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes home' looks like carrying something; it means earning after tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonnets are fourteen-line poems.

clue.text: Powerful woman in secret society snubbed during parade

indicators.note: snubbed suggests something cut short, so the last letter goes
during places the shortened society inside the other word

blocks.note: a march is a parade
a Triad is a Chinese secret criminal society

explanation.surface: A powerful woman in a secret society is ignored at a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is a woman who heads a family or group, a figure of authority.

clue.text: Irregular bears a sword

indicators.note: irregular means not in the usual order, so the letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An irregular soldier carries a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' looks like a guerrilla fighter carrying the weapon; it is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabre is a heavy cavalry sword with a curved blade.

clue.text: Bob breaking rule causes one to stand down

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

blocks.note: to reign is to rule
a bob was a shilling, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: Bob broke the rules, and that forces someone to step down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; a bob was the old British shilling, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up a post, i.e. stand down.

clue.text: Decidedly trendy suit

blocks.note: in means fashionable
spades is one of the four card suits

explanation.surface: A firmly fashionable suit of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing; it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In spades is an idiom meaning to a great degree, emphatically.
